title: Google Deepmind's "Humanity's First Exam" shows top AI models still fail simple everyday tasks under repeated runs
excerpt:
Google Deepmind tests the reliability of 18 AI models with "Humanity's First Exam." Top models solve nearly every task family at least once, but even leaders like OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra stumble when asked for 16 straight correct answers. Visual perception accounts for 73 percent of errors, and more compute time doesn't fix the problem.
The article Google Deepmind's "Humanity's First Exam" shows top AI models still fail simple everyday tasks under repeated runs appeared first on The Decoder .

ai.summary: DeepMind evaluated 18 AI models on a "Humanity's First Exam" and found that even top models failed to answer 16 consecutive questions correctly, with 73% of errors stemming from visual perception tasks.
ai.why: Reveals reliability gaps that developers must consider when deploying multimodal models.

title: Poetry for Engineers: Prompt Engineering for Odysseus
excerpt:
I. Odysseus asks the oracle:
Shortest route to Ithaca?
Avoid Cyclops.
Avoid Sirens.
Prefer ferries with Wi-Fi.
The oracle thinks for three seconds:
Recalculating...
Thinking...
Would you like a more scenic route?
II.
Odysseus tries again:
Tell me what lies beyond the known world.
The oracle offers twelve sources,
three maps, two warnings,
and one confident island
that has never existed.
Odysseus mutters to himself:
Oh Muse, yet again
the oracle is hallucinating...
The oracle continues:
Look, I know a special place on Kefalonia,
and a few tricks to get you back home.
Would you like me to continue?
III.
So Odysseus asks his final question:
If I can know everything,
why do I still need to…

ai.summary: The article presents a poetic dialogue illustrating the challenges of prompt engineering, using the myth of Odysseus and an oracle that hallucinates answers.

title: Terence Tao sees AI ushering in "Big Math," but calls major tech firms' proofs "toxic waste"
excerpt:
Terence Tao outlines his vision of "Big Math" on the Hard Fork podcast. Instead of solo work, human-AI teams would systematically map thousands of problems. He also calls AI proofs from major tech companies "toxic waste," saying the models solve problems but can't explain their results. Tao hopes for a new division of labor where AI delivers the first rough solution and humans put it in context.
